title: Understanding AI Agents: Goals, Tools, and Actions
introduction: In this lesson you will learn what an AI agent is, how it uses goals, tools, memory, and actions, and how it differs from a simple chatbot.

sections.heading: What Is an AI Agent?
sections.subheading: A system that can act to achieve a goal
paragraphs: An AI agent is a computer program that can sense its environment, think using a model, and take actions to reach a specific goal.
It is more than just answering questions; it can plan and act over time.

example.title: Smart Home Assistant
example.content: A smart home assistant can turn lights on, adjust temperature, and order groceries automatically based on your preferences.

sections.heading: Goals and Actions
sections.subheading: Defining what the agent wants to achieve
paragraphs: The goal is the desired outcome the agent works toward, such as keeping a room clean.
Actions are the steps the agent can perform, like moving forward, picking up objects, or sending a command.

example.title: Robot Vacuum Cleaner
example.content: The robot vacuum’s goal is a clean floor. Its actions include moving, detecting dirt, and returning to the charging dock.

sections.heading: Tools and Memory
sections.subheading: Resources the agent uses to think and act
paragraphs: Tools are external services or devices the agent can call, like a weather API or a camera.
Memory lets the agent store information from past interactions, helping it make better decisions later.

example.title: Travel Planning AI
example.content: The AI uses a map service (tool) to find routes and remembers your past trips (memory) to suggest better itineraries.

sections.heading: Agent Loop vs. Simple Chatbot
sections.subheading: Continuous decision making compared to single replies
paragraphs: An agent runs an ongoing loop: observe, think, act, then observe again.
A chatbot typically receives a message, generates one reply, and stops until the next message.
The loop lets agents act autonomously without waiting for new user input each time.

example.title: Customer Support Bot vs. AI Agent
example.content: A support chatbot answers one question at a time. An AI agent could monitor a system, detect issues, and automatically restart services without being asked.

practice.title: Spot an AI Agent Around You
practice.instruction: Identify a device or service you use that can act on its own to meet a goal. Write down its goal, at least one tool it uses, and one action it performs.

keyTakeaways: An AI agent is a system that can perceive, think, and act to achieve a specific goal.
Agents use tools, memory, and actions, and they operate in a continuous loop.
Unlike a simple chatbot, an AI agent can act autonomously over time.

mcqs.question: What is the main difference between an AI agent and a simple chatbot?
options: An AI agent can act autonomously over time without waiting for new input.
An AI agent can only answer one question at a time.
An AI agent cannot use external services.
An AI agent does not have any memory.
mcqs.explanation: AI agents run a continuous loop of observe‑think‑act, allowing them to take actions on their own, while chatbots reply once and wait for the next user message.

mcqs.question: In the robot vacuum cleaner example, which of the following is an action the agent can perform?
options: Moving across the floor to clean
mcqs.explanation: Moving across the floor is a direct physical step the vacuum takes to achieve its goal of a clean floor.

mcqs.question: Which component lets an AI agent store information from past interactions?
mcqs.explanation: Memory is the part of an agent that records previous data, helping it make better decisions later.

mcqs.question: What is the correct order of steps in the agent loop?
mcqs.explanation: The loop starts with observing the environment, then thinking (planning), and finally acting.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of a tool an AI agent might use?
mcqs.explanation: A map service is an external resource that the agent can call to help it plan routes, fitting the definition of a tool.
